facts.fact: The African Development Bank approved a $1 million grant, run by UNHCR with the Togolese authorities over twelve months, that will support the registration and documentation of 5,000 new arrivals in the Savanes region.
facts.system: registration and documentation of new arrivals

facts.fact: CNAR and UNHCR trained all CNAR technical staff and external data-entry operators on 2-3 August 2025 in Kara to enter socio-economic data for refugees and asylum seekers in CNAR's ProGres V4 registration database.
CNAR states that after four registration operations between 2023 and 2025, 41,773 Burkinabe officially obtained refugee status in Togo.
CNAR states a decentralised operation from 22 May to 16 July 2025 produced and distributed 10,972 refugee identity cards in the Savanes region, produced by the DGDN.

facts.fact: CNAR, PURS and ANID began on 10 May 2024 an operation (2 May to 29 August 2024) to register new Burkinabe asylum-seekers and distribute identification cards to displaced people already enrolled, updating the CNAR proGres v4 database.

UNHCR says CNAR has run a biometric registration exercise in the Savanes region since 24 May 2026, registering 3,999 previously unregistered people, with 1,958 still unregistered at end June 2026, while identity card issuance is stalled for lack of materials.

systems.system: CNAR registration (Coordination Nationale d'Assistance aux Refugies)

facts.fact: UNHCR reports that registration capacities were gradually strengthened in Benin and Togo in 2024, and about 6,200 IDPs were registered in Togo and Benin during the year.

note: Support to about 48,000 displaced people and refugees is stated without registration, documents or digital services.
